steps.title: Prove the proposition, activation and survey-optimisation model
steps.summary: Keep Year 1 deliberately focused while the wider graduate premium evidence and content estate is still being built. Define the student-facing King’s Edge and graduate premium proposition, map the most important points in the student journey and test internal activation in a small number of priority settings. Make Graduate Outcomes response-rate optimisation the flagship survey intervention: use existing intelligence to identify areas where positive destinations appear strong but response is weaker than it should be, target engagement accordingly and evaluate what moves response. In parallel, map the small number of other surveys with material outcomes or reputation value, understand their mechanics and audiences, establish external perception baselines and test early messages using the first assets emerging from 2.4.1 rather than launching a large external campaign prematurely.

outputs.title: Student proposition and activation model
outputs.summary: A clear student-facing King’s Edge and graduate premium proposition, mapped to priority student-journey touchpoints with an initial set of staff-facing language, prompts and activation pilots.

outputs.title: Graduate Outcomes optimisation pilot and strategic survey map
outputs.summary: A targeted GO response-rate intervention model focused on high-value opportunities for improvement, together with a prioritised map of other outcomes, employability and reputation surveys, their mechanics, audiences and plausible intervention levers.

outputs.title: External audience and reputation activation baseline
outputs.summary: A prioritised view of external audiences, current perceptions, early message tests and the activation opportunities that should be developed as the 2.4.1 evidence and content estate matures.

steps.title: Scale student adoption and test external reputation activation
steps.summary: Scale the strongest Year 1 student proposition and adoption approaches through onboarding, advising, Careers, faculty activity, digital touchpoints and other major student moments, using the developing King’s Canvas, portal and academic-year rhythm where they add value. Industrialise the Graduate Outcomes optimisation model across priority departments and cohorts and establish repeatable evaluation of interventions. Use the broader 2.4.1 asset estate and 2.4.2 external validation to run targeted external activation with priority applicant, family, employer, alumni, international and sector audiences, testing which messages, channels, advocates and partnerships create measurable reputation or market traction.

outputs.title: Scaled student adoption model
outputs.summary: The graduate premium proposition is activated consistently through a broader set of student-facing channels, moments and staff communities, with early evidence about recognition and engagement.

outputs.title: Scaled Graduate Outcomes response-optimisation cycle
outputs.summary: A repeatable model for identifying high-value response opportunities, targeting interventions, monitoring response and learning what works across priority areas.

outputs.title: Targeted external reputation pilots
outputs.summary: A portfolio of audience-specific activation tests using evidence-backed 2.4.1 assets, employer and alumni advocacy, recruitment and international channels, partnerships and selected sector-facing activity.

steps.title: Embed adoption, reputation and strategic survey performance
steps.summary: Use the final mobilisation year to embed the strongest approaches rather than simply increasing campaign volume. Make the graduate premium proposition part of normal student-facing practice and the institutional rhythm, with sustained staff adoption and clear links into the wider King’s Edge experience. Scale external reputation approaches that have demonstrated traction, including employer and alumni advocacy, recruitment and international activation, partnerships, PR and sector-facing activity, drawing on the now-mature 2.4.1 asset estate and 2.4.2 validation. Establish a repeatable annual strategic survey-performance cycle covering Graduate Outcomes and the small number of priority employability and reputation surveys, with clear ownership, intervention plans, evaluation and continuous refinement.

outputs.summary: The proposition is sustained through normal student-facing channels, staff practice and institutional rhythms rather than relying primarily on standalone campaign activity.

outputs.title: Scaled reputation and market activation model
outputs.summary: The external approaches that have demonstrated value are integrated into ongoing recruitment, communications, employer, alumni, partnership and sector activity with clear audience priorities and stewardship.

outputs.title: Annual strategic survey-performance cycle
outputs.summary: Graduate Outcomes and priority external employability and reputation surveys have understood mechanics, explicit performance strategies, named institutional partners, targeted interventions and an annual evaluate-and-refine cycle.
